preferences.title: All strict compiler options on
preferences.statement: Enable `strict` plus the strictness flags it leaves out: `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noImplicitOverride`, `noImplicitReturns`, `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch`.
preferences.why: The compiler catches whole classes of bugs (unchecked index access, missing returns, implicit any) before review does.
preferences.notes: `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` is left out on purpose: it rejects the `email: row.email ?? undefined` mapper pattern unless every optional property is typed `T | undefined`. `strict` includes `useUnknownInCatchVariables`, so `catch (error)` gives `unknown`; narrow before reading `.message`.

preferences.title: No `any`
preferences.statement: Never use `any`. Type values explicitly, or use `unknown` and narrow.
preferences.why: `any` switches type checking off silently, and the hole spreads to everything the value touches.

preferences.title: No `null`: `undefined` only
preferences.statement: Never use `null` in application code; `undefined` is the only absence value. Convert `null` to `undefined` at every boundary (API responses, database rows) with `value ?? undefined`, usually in a mapper.
preferences.why: One absence value means one check (`?.`, `??`, `=== undefined`), and optional properties (`x?: T`) already mean `undefined`.
preferences.notes: Still allowed where a platform API demands it: `Object.create(null)`, `useRef(null)`, `JSON.stringify(x, null, 2)`, `insertBefore(node, null)`, `setPrototypeOf(x, null)`. React 18+ components can `return undefined`. Boundary code that must read or write `null` (ORM entities, raw API types) gets a path exemption in `.js-ts-conventions/overrides.json`.

preferences.title: Explicit types at module boundaries
preferences.statement: Exported functions and public methods declare their parameter and return types.
preferences.why: From "explicitly type everything": the signature is the contract, so inference must not change it silently.

preferences.title: Naming conventions
preferences.statement: PascalCase for classes, interfaces, types, enums and type parameters. SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE for enum members. camelCase for functions, methods, properties, parameters and variables (PascalCase is fine for React components, and for schema or class values such as `CreateRequestDtoSchema`).
preferences.why: The case of a name tells the reader what kind of thing it is before they look it up.
preferences.notes: Shorthand destructuring (`const { first_name } = row`), object keys and imports mirror external shapes and are not checked.

preferences.title: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE constants
preferences.statement: Module-level constants holding a primitive literal are SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE.
preferences.why: Constants read as configuration at a glance, separate from values computed at runtime.
preferences.notes: Framework-mandated exports keep their names (`dynamic`, `revalidate`, `runtime`, `prerender`, ...). Add more via `options.constant-case.allow` in overrides.

preferences.title: kebab-case filenames
preferences.statement: Filenames are kebab-case, with dot-separated role suffixes: `request.entity.ts`, `create-request.command.ts`, `request-status.value-object.ts`.
preferences.why: One casing works on every filesystem and makes the role of a file greppable.

preferences.title: Explicit methods, not getters
preferences.statement: Expose state through explicit methods (`getFirstName()`, `isValid()`), never class `get` accessors.
preferences.why: A method call says work may happen; a getter disguises computation as a field read.

preferences.title: Value object structure
preferences.statement: Value objects have a private constructor, validate in a protected `validate()`, are created through a static `create()` that returns a `Result`, and expose values through explicit methods (`getValue()`).
preferences.why: Construction always goes through validation, and callers handle failure as a value instead of a surprise throw.
preferences.review: Sample up to 10 classes extending `ValueObject` (or living in `value-objects/`). Check: private constructor, protected `validate()`, static `create()` returning `Result`, explicit getter methods, readonly props.

preferences.title: `Result` for fallible operations
preferences.statement: Factories and repository methods that can fail return the repo's `Result<T, E>` instead of throwing. Callers check `isErr()` before `getValue()`.
preferences.why: Failure becomes part of the signature, so the compiler makes every caller handle it.
preferences.review: Find the repo's Result type (grep `Result.ok(`). Sample up to 10 static `create()` factories and repository `find*`/`save*` methods: fallible ones return `Result`. Never introduce a second Result library.

preferences.title: Zod validation at every boundary
preferences.statement: Validate all external input (request DTOs, webhook payloads, third-party API responses, env) with a Zod schema, and derive the TypeScript type with `z.infer`; never hand-write a parallel interface.
preferences.why: Types describe what you hope arrives; schemas check what actually arrived.
preferences.review: List entry points (controllers, route handlers, server actions, webhook handlers, API clients). Sample up to 10: each parses input through a Zod schema before use, and DTO types come from `z.infer`.

preferences.title: ISO standards for international data
preferences.statement: Dates and times are ISO 8601 strings (`toISOString()`, `z.string().datetime()`). Phone numbers are E.164 (`+32470123456`). Countries are ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (`BE`). Languages are ISO 639-1 (`fr`), and locales combine them (`fr-BE`).
preferences.why: One canonical format per kind of data removes parsing ambiguity between services, databases and locales.
preferences.review: Grep schemas and DTOs for date, phone, country, language and locale fields. Check their validators: `.datetime()`, an E.164 regex, ISO code enums. Flag `toLocaleDateString()` or custom date formats in stored or transmitted data.

preferences.title: Readonly properties
preferences.statement: Mark properties `readonly`: interface and type members, class fields and constructor parameter properties. Leave a class field mutable only when the class reassigns it.
preferences.why: Immutable data can be shared and reasoned about without defensive copies.

preferences.title: `as const` for constant collections
preferences.statement: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE array and object constants end with `as const`.
preferences.why: The value becomes deeply read-only and keeps its literal types, so `(typeof REQUEST_TYPES)[number]` is a precise union.

preferences.title: Typed exceptions
preferences.statement: Domain, application and infrastructure code throws typed exceptions (`ArgumentInvalidException`, `EntityNotFoundException`, `ConflictException`, ...), never a bare `Error`. A global exception filter maps them to HTTP status codes.
preferences.why: The exception type carries the meaning, and the filter turns it into the right status code (400, 404, 409) in one place.
preferences.bad: throw new Error('Email cannot be empty');
preferences.good:
throw new ArgumentInvalidException('Email cannot be empty');
throw new EntityNotFoundException('Contact not found');
preferences.review: Check that one global filter maps domain exceptions to HTTP codes (NestJS: `@Catch(DomainException, HttpException)`).

preferences.title: `@/` alias for cross-module imports
preferences.statement: Import across modules through the `@/` path alias. Relative paths are for the same folder or one level up only.
preferences.why: Alias paths survive file moves and show where a dependency lives.
preferences.good:
import { Command } from '@/libs/ddd/command.base';
import { RequestEntity } from '@/modules/sales/request/domain/request.entity';
preferences.notes: Enforced only where a tsconfig defines an `@/*` path alias. Without one, adding the alias is a config step in the fix plan. Tooling configs (`*.config.*`) are exempt.

preferences.title: `import type` for type-only imports
preferences.statement: Use a separate `import type` for anything used only as a type; use regular imports for classes and values.
preferences.why: Type-only imports are erased predictably, which avoids accidental runtime cycles and side-effect imports.
preferences.good:
import type { CreateRequestDto } from './create-request.request.dto';
import { CreateRequestCommand } from './create-request.command';
preferences.notes: NestJS with `emitDecoratorMetadata`: constructor-injected classes must stay value imports. ESLint skips decorated files when the decorator parser options are set (this skill sets them). oxlint has no such check, so DI-role files (`*.controller.ts`, `*.service.ts`, ...) are exempt there.

preferences.title: JSDoc on public APIs
preferences.statement: Exported functions, classes and public methods carry a JSDoc block: purpose, `@param`, `@returns`, and `@throws` (or "never throws, returns Result").
preferences.why: The contract shows in editor hovers without opening the implementation.
preferences.bad: public static create(props: RequestProps): Result<Request, string> {}
preferences.good:
/**
 * Creates a new visit request.
 *
 * @param props - Request properties including dealId, contactId and type
 * @returns Result containing the created Request or an error message
 * @throws Never throws - returns Result instead
 */
public static create(props: RequestProps): Result<Request, string> {}
preferences.review: Sample up to 10 exported functions or classes in domain and application code; report the share with a JSDoc block.

preferences.title: Comments explain why, not what
preferences.statement: Inline comments explain intent, constraints or trade-offs. Code that needs a "what" comment gets clearer names instead.
preferences.why: "What" comments repeat the code and rot; "why" comments carry knowledge the code cannot.
preferences.bad:
// Multiply attempt by attempt by 1000
await this.delay(attempt * attempt * 1000);
preferences.good:
// Exponential backoff so we don't overwhelm the API during outages
await this.delay(attempt * attempt * 1000);
preferences.review: Skim the comments in 5 recently changed files and note any that restate the code.
